title: Another approach gives growth greater freedom
meaning: A wish to nurture usefulness may inspire a change of approach and a sense of freedom around familiar attachments.
text: Development becomes more substantial when a familiar method stops seeming the only possibility. The Empress in the energy of Sahasrara supports a wish to nurture useful experience and help interest find living continuation. The Hanged Man in the physical position describes actions: changing viewpoints, reshaping a familiar activity and setting aside a ready answer for another understanding. The Devil in emotions brings clear freedom to notice attachments and retain choice. Your contribution can make this freedom available through other people’s actual experience rather than leaving it only in ideas you discuss privately together.

For example, you help at an open session for making small collages. Instead of offering a model to repeat, you arrange scraps by texture and suggest an unexpected combination as a beginning. **Another approach lets growth move beyond a familiar model.** Someone notices they can choose differently and still create meaningful work. You enjoy that independence, which can continue without treating a particular purchased kit or a leader’s approval as a condition of beginning.

Things become harder if abandoning ready models also removes any understandable way for a beginner to join materials. Available choices become practically inaccessible. A creative motive and clear freedom remain supportive. Action benefits from passing on a simple foundation: another view releases people from a single result when they also understand how to make an attempt of their own.
